paper.title_en: Cancellation of cryocooler-induced vibration in trapped-ion systems
paper.abstract_en: Mechanical cryocoolers offer numerous benefits for the operation of vacuum systems containing trapped atomic ions. However, the fidelity of laser-based gates can be degraded by phase noise induced by the cryocooler vibrations. We present a feed-forward vibration-cancellation system that directly measures inner shield displacement with an auxiliary interferometer and applies a compensating phase correction to the laser drive. The interferometer signal is demodulated, and a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) system unwraps the displacement measurement signal, computes the required correction phase, and updates the RF drive of an in-line acousto-optic modulator (AOM) to correct for the vibration-induced dephasing. With cancellation active, the qubit coherence time improves from $3.0\pm0.4$ ms to $35\pm5$ ms, consistent with a simulation based on the measured vibration spectrum. We further validate the cancellation by artificially increasing the mechanical coupling of the cryocooler to the vacuum chamber. The vibration-induced decoherence rate is suppressed by a factor of approximately 70 at an RMS (root mean square) displacement of 0.65 $\mathrmμ$m.
